subject: Environment
description: Covers UNFCCC, Kyoto, Paris, Montreal, Kigali, and Loss and Damage.

questions.stem: The Kyoto Protocol (1997) operationalized the UNFCCC by committing industrialized countries to limit and reduce greenhouse gases. What was the central principle of this protocol?

options.option_text: Common but Differentiated Responsibilities (CBDR), placing the heavier burden on developed nations
Equal Percentage Reductions (EPR) for all signatory nations regardless of development status
Polluter Pays Principle applied exclusively to fossil fuel extracting corporations
Voluntary Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs) without binding legal targets

questions.explanation: KYOTO PROTOCOL: Adopted in 1997, entered into force in 2005. Its core principle was "Common but Differentiated Responsibilities and Respective Capabilities" (CBDR-RC). Because developed nations (Annex I) are principally responsible for the current high levels of GHG emissions in the atmosphere due to 150+ years of industrial activity, the Protocol placed a heavier, legally binding burden on them. Developing nations (like India and China) were exempt from binding emission reduction targets. NDCs are the hallmark of the Paris Agreement, not Kyoto. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims, SSC CGL.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The Paris Agreement (2015) aims to strengthen the global response to the threat of climate change by keeping a global temperature rise this century well below:

options.option_text: 2 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels, while pursuing efforts to limit it to 1.5 degrees Celsius
1.5 degrees Celsius above 1990 levels, with a hard cap at 2 degrees
3 degrees Celsius above pre-industrial levels
0 degrees Celsius change from the year 2000 levels

questions.explanation: PARIS AGREEMENT GOAL: Article 2 sets the temperature goal: "Holding the increase in the global average temperature to well below 2°C above pre-industrial levels and pursuing efforts to limit the temperature increase to 1.5°C." It also aims to increase the ability to adapt to adverse impacts of climate change and make finance flows consistent with low GHG emissions. Unlike Kyoto, Paris is based on bottom-up "Nationally Determined Contributions" (NDCs) submitted by ALL countries, not just developed ones. PYQ FREQUENCY: Highly repeated across all exams.

questions.stem: Which international treaty specifically targets the phase-out of Ozone Depleting Substances (ODS) such as CFCs and HCFCs?

options.option_text: Montreal Protocol
Kyoto Protocol
Stockholm Convention
Basel Convention

questions.explanation: MONTREAL PROTOCOL: Adopted in 1987, it is an international treaty designed to protect the ozone layer by phasing out the production of numerous substances that are responsible for ozone depletion (like Chlorofluorocarbons - CFCs, and Halons). It is widely considered the most successful environmental treaty in history, achieving universal ratification. KYOTO: Greenhouse gases. STOCKHOLM: Persistent Organic Pollutants (POPs). BASEL: Transboundary movement of hazardous wastes. PYQ FREQUENCY: SSC CGL, RRB NTPC, UPSC GS-3.
questions.subject: Environment

questions.stem: The Kigali Amendment (2016) to the Montreal Protocol aims to phase down the production and consumption of which specific class of gases?

options.option_text: Hydrofluorocarbons (HFCs), which are potent greenhouse gases though they do not deplete the ozone layer
Chlorofluorocarbons (CFCs), extending the original Montreal deadlines
Sulphur Dioxide (SO2) from coal power plants
Methane (CH4) emissions from agriculture and waste

questions.explanation: KIGALI AMENDMENT (2016): A legally binding amendment to the Montreal Protocol. HFCs were introduced as non-ozone-depleting alternatives to CFCs and HCFCs. However, HFCs are extremely potent greenhouse gases (with high Global Warming Potential). The Kigali Amendment aims to phase down HFCs by 80-85% by the late 2040s, bridging the gap between ozone protection and climate change mitigation. It could prevent up to 0.5°C of global warming by 2100. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims, State PSCs.

questions.stem: Under the UNFCCC, what is the purpose of the "Loss and Damage" fund, formally agreed upon at COP27 in Sharm el-Sheikh?

options.option_text: To provide financial assistance to vulnerable developing countries suffering from unavoidable climate change impacts like rising sea levels and extreme weather
To compensate fossil fuel companies for stranded assets as the world transitions to renewable energy
To fund the research and development of carbon capture and storage technologies in developed nations
To penalize countries that fail to meet their Nationally Determined Contributions (NDCs)

questions.explanation: LOSS AND DAMAGE FUND: A landmark decision at COP27 (2022) in Egypt. "Loss and Damage" refers to the destructive impacts of climate change that cannot be avoided either by mitigation (reducing emissions) or adaptation (preparing for impacts). It involves historical responsibility — developed nations historically emitted the most, but developing, vulnerable nations (like small island states) suffer the most. The fund aims to rescue and rebuild these vulnerable nations. It was operationalized at COP28 in Dubai. PYQ FREQUENCY: Current Affairs, UPSC Prelims.

questions.stem: Which of the following was the FIRST global conference on the environment that led to the creation of the United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP)?

options.option_text: Stockholm Conference (1972)
Earth Summit / Rio Conference (1992)
Kyoto Conference (1997)
Geneva Climate Conference (1979)

questions.explanation: STOCKHOLM CONFERENCE 1972: The United Nations Conference on the Human Environment in Stockholm, Sweden, was the first major international conference on environmental issues. It resulted in the Stockholm Declaration containing 26 principles. Most importantly, it led to the creation of UNEP (headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya). The Rio Earth Summit happened 20 years later (1992) and produced the UNFCCC, CBD, and UNCCD. PYQ FREQUENCY: SSC CGL, State PSCs, UPSC.

questions.stem: Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) and Joint Implementation (JI) are carbon market mechanisms originally established under which treaty?

options.option_text: Kyoto Protocol
Paris Agreement
Montreal Protocol
Cartagena Protocol

questions.explanation:
KYOTO MECHANISMS: The Kyoto Protocol defined three "flexible mechanisms" to help Annex I (developed) countries meet their emission targets cost-effectively:
1. Clean Development Mechanism (CDM): Developed countries fund emission-reduction projects in developing countries and earn Certified Emission Reduction (CER) credits.
2. Joint Implementation (JI): A developed country invests in an emission-reduction project in another developed country.
3. Emissions Trading: Buying and selling carbon credits among developed countries. 
Under the Paris Agreement, new market mechanisms are being negotiated under Article 6. PYQ FREQUENCY: UPSC Prelims, IFS.

questions.stem: The Green Climate Fund (GCF), the UNFCCC's primary dedicated fund for climate action in developing countries, is permanently headquartered in which city?

options.option_text: Geneva, Switzerland — seat of many UN specialized agencies
Songdo, South Korea — the GCF's official home since 2012
Bonn, Germany — where the UNFCCC Secretariat is based
Nairobi, Kenya — headquarters of UNEP and UN-Habitat

questions.explanation: B is correct because the GCF Board selected Songdo (Incheon), South Korea as its permanent host city in 2012 and signed a Host Country Agreement with the Republic of Korea. Geneva is a common distractor as it hosts many UN bodies, but the GCF was deliberately placed in Asia to signal proximity to the most climate-vulnerable developing regions.

questions.stem: The UNFCCC established two permanent Subsidiary Bodies to support the Conference of Parties. Which one is specifically mandated to provide timely scientific, technological, and methodological advice to the COP?

options.option_text: Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC)
Subsidiary Body for Scientific and Technological Advice (SBSTA)
Global Environment Facility (GEF) Scientific Committee
Technology Executive Committee under the UNFCCC framework

questions.explanation: B is correct because the SBSTA is one of the two permanent subsidiary bodies created by the UNFCCC (the other being SBI — Subsidiary Body for Implementation) and directly advises the COP on science and technology. The IPCC (Option A) is the most tempting wrong answer: it is a joint body of WMO and UNEP, established in 1988, and is NOT formally a UNFCCC body — it provides external scientific assessments that COP may draw upon.

questions.stem: Under the Paris Agreement's built-in ambition mechanism, each Party must communicate or update its Nationally Determined Contribution (NDC) at a fixed interval. What is that interval, and what constraint applies to each successive NDC?

options.option_text: Every 3 years; the new NDC must cover at least 10 additional years
Every 5 years; each successive NDC must represent a progression
Every 10 years, aligned with the decadal Long-Term Strategy cycle
Every 2 years, co-submitted alongside Biennial Transparency Reports

questions.explanation: B is correct: Article 4.9 of the Paris Agreement requires Parties to communicate NDCs every five years, and Article 4.3 mandates that each successive NDC must represent a progression beyond the current one. Option D is a common trap — Biennial Transparency Reports (BTRs) are submitted every 2 years under the Enhanced Transparency Framework, but NDCs follow a separate 5-year 'ratchet' cycle aligned with the Global Stocktake.

questions.stem: The Adaptation Fund finances climate adaptation projects in vulnerable developing countries. What is the unique source that originally provided a share of its capitalisation under the Kyoto Protocol?

options.option_text: Joint Implementation Emission Reduction Units traded among Annex I
Voluntary credits listed on the Chicago Climate Exchange platform
A 2% levy on Certified Emission Reductions (CERs) from CDM projects
Technology transfer grants disbursed by the Global Environment Facility

questions.explanation: C is correct: the Adaptation Fund was capitalised through a 2% share of proceeds (SOP) deducted from each CER issued under the Clean Development Mechanism (CDM) of the Kyoto Protocol — a novel market-linked financing model. Option A is the key distractor: JI generates ERUs (not CERs) and its proceeds do NOT fund the Adaptation Fund. The AF has since also received pledges from developed-country governments, especially post-Paris.

questions.stem: CORSIA (Carbon Offsetting and Reduction Scheme for International Aviation), adopted in 2016 to stabilise net CO₂ emissions from international flights at 2020 levels, operates under the authority of which intergovernmental body?

options.option_text: UNFCCC directly, as Paris Agreement explicitly covers aviation sectors
International Maritime Organization, regulator of global transport modes
International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO), a UN specialised agency
World Meteorological Organization, given aviation's atmospheric linkages

questions.explanation: C is correct: CORSIA was adopted by the 39th Session of ICAO Assembly in 2016, since international aviation emissions are explicitly excluded from national NDCs under the Paris Agreement and fall under ICAO's mandate. Option A is the most seductive wrong answer — the Paris Agreement does NOT cover international aviation; that gap is precisely why a separate ICAO-led scheme was needed. The IMO separately handles shipping via its Initial GHG Strategy.

questions.stem: The Glasgow Climate Pact (COP26, 2021) was historic as the first COP decision text to explicitly name a fossil fuel. The final wording was diluted from 'phase out' to 'phase down' at the insistence of which country, and what was the exact phrase used?

options.option_text: China insisted; final text reads 'phase down unabated coal power'
India insisted; final text reads 'phase down unabated coal power'
Saudi Arabia insisted; final text reads 'phase out inefficient oil subsidies'
Australia insisted; final text reads 'phase down unabated fossil fuels'

questions.explanation: B is correct: India, backed by China, secured the last-minute change from 'phase out' to 'phase down' of 'unabated coal power' in the Glasgow Climate Pact, causing visible distress to COP26 President Alok Sharma. The exact phrase in paragraph 36 is 'phase down unabated coal power and phase out inefficient fossil fuel subsidies.' Option A (China) is the chief distractor since China also supported the change, but it was India's Environment Minister Bhupender Yadav who formally moved the amendment on the floor.

questions.stem: Under Article 14 of the Paris Agreement, the Global Stocktake (GST) is a periodic assessment of collective progress. The first GST concluded at COP28 (Dubai, 2023) found the world 'not on track' for 1.5°C. What is the primary institutional purpose of the GST output?

options.option_text: Imposing binding financial penalties on Parties that missed their NDC targets
Informing the preparation of each Party's subsequent, more ambitious NDC
Negotiating legally binding emission caps under a new Kyoto-style protocol
Determining the quantum of Loss and Damage finance owed by historic emitters

questions.explanation: B is correct: Article 14.3 explicitly states that the outcome of the Global Stocktake shall 'inform Parties in updating and enhancing, in a nationally determined manner, their actions and support.' The GST identifies the collective ambition gap so that each Party's next 5-year NDC (due 2025) can be more ambitious. Option A is wrong because the Paris Agreement contains no compliance penalties — its enforcement is through transparency and peer pressure. Option C conflates the GST with treaty negotiation; no new binding protocol emerges from it.
